rationale: The drain-burst experiment executed (receipt 7e046ae9ebb44e58bb2a4800bdf14ef3, experiment ba4b0efa5ad64f069964ee92cc43b432-experiment, status completed, outcome tests_passed, exit 0, no changed target files) and I read its receipt before writing. All three drain comparisons hold with complete admissions: admission index 5 records the accumulated queue (pending=64, committed=0, in_term=false, unconfirmed=0) and result index 6 records the single commit step finishing with pending=0, unconfirmed=64, broadcasts=64, committed=1 and in_term=true. The same invocation also re-measured the earlier paths (indices 1-2 queued, 4 admitted), so one receipt now carries the whole predicate. I promote the drain to a durable fact and revise the interpretation to cite this receipt, which converts the previously source-only consequence (the retained queue turning into a burst of outbound messages on release) into a measured one.

knowledge.statement: When a two-voter leader that has accumulated 64 queued read requests (pendingReadIndexMessages length 64, committed 0, committedEntryInCurrentTerm() false, unconfirmedReads 0) finally commits in its term through the normal MsgAppResp fast path, that single step empties the queue and re-admits everything: pendingReadIndexMessages becomes 0, readOnly.unconfirmedReads becomes 64 and 64 MsgHeartbeat messages are produced in the same step, with committed 1 and in_term true afterwards. So the retained queue is not merely passive memory: on release it becomes one read request plus one outbound heartbeat per queued entry, all at once.
knowledge.conditions: Library defaults (CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe); the commit is produced by stepping the leader's own MsgAppResp and then node 2's MsgAppResp at lastIndex, which is the call site that invokes releasePendingReadIndexMessages - the harness never calls the release function directly. No heartbeat response is delivered afterwards, so the re-admitted requests stay unconfirmed.

interpretations.rationale: Final measured revision of this question; one receipt now covers every part of the predicate. Receipt 7e046ae9ebb44e58bb2a4800bdf14ef3 (experiment ba4b0efa5ad64f069964ee92cc43b432-experiment) ran in the isolated workspace; status completed, outcome tests_passed, exit 0, no changed target files, no parsing errors. Decisive parsed indices: 1 and 2 are the quorum-less leader (StateLeader, term 1, committed 0, lastIndex 1, CheckQuorum false, ReadOnlySafe, three voters) with 64 same-context retries producing pending 64, unconfirmed 0, and pending still 64 after a higher-term heartbeat made it a follower; 3 and 4 are the two-voter leader committed in its term (committed 1, in_term true) whose 64 retries produced unconfirmed 64 and broadcasts 64 with confirmed 0; 5 and 6 are the drain case, where 64 queued requests (pending 64, committed 0, in_term false) became, in the single commit step, pending 0, unconfirmed 64, broadcasts 64 with committed 1 and in_term true. All seven declared comparisons across the three executions of this investigation evaluated holds with comparison_complete true and no missing indices. What this revision adds: the consequence is no longer only retention - the retained queue converts, at the moment the leader becomes able to commit, into a burst of one admission and one outbound heartbeat per queued entry, all in one step, which is the amplification the earlier revision stated from source. The scoped defect claim is unchanged and still asserted: under permitted conditions (legitimate leader; CheckQuorum false, the library default, not required by ReadOnlySafe; a caller following the documented unbounded retry advice at node.go:218-224; and either a missing term-commit or missing heartbeat acknowledgements) the library retains one read request per retry with no collapsing, never reclaims it (raft.reset leaves the queue; only a quorum ack advances maybeAdvance for admitted ones), and can emit one heartbeat per retry - both while accumulating and again as a single burst when the queue is released. The refusal to answer reads without quorum remains correct and is not the complaint; the missing library-side bound, the unreclaimed retention, and the retry-proportional message emission are. Counterevidence considered and not defeating: a healthy quorum confirms each retry on the next heartbeat response, so this is not a steady-state cost; the removal of context-keyed handling is the v3.7.0 stale-index fix (CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-3.7.md, PR 397) and is not contested, only the absence of a size limit around it; a caller that retries without bound recreates its own obligation, but no bound is stated and the caller gets no signal that its request is still queued. Severity remains explicitly unassessed: no footprint measurement, no OOM and no liveness failure is claimed, and the burst is measured in one configuration at one queue depth.

knowledge.assertion: the commit step drains the whole queued set at once, re-admitting each entry and emitting one heartbeat per entry
the queued path accumulates one pending entry per retry and is not reclaimed by deposition
admission is per request and context-blind on both paths

limitations: Severity is unassessed: the claim is that the library imposes no bound, never reclaims the state, and emits one heartbeat per retry (plus a burst on release), not that a given deployment exhausts memory or saturates its transport.

The experiments drive direct raft instances with no responses delivered, so the triggers (partition from quorum, or loss of heartbeat acknowledgements, both with CheckQuorum disabled) are modelled rather than exercised over a network.
etcd's own retry policy was not examined, so the practical retry bound in the primary downstream user is unknown.

Each measurement uses one configuration at one depth (64 retries); linearity in the retry count follows from the mechanism (one append per admitted request, looped release) rather than from a sweep of depths.
